topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text: The earth whispered secrets as I dug, loose soil parting like a forgotten book. The object I unearthed, smoother than memory, colder than lost time, was a box, or was it always a chest? I do not recall its burial, yet here it lies, heavy with the breath of years. Its lid, when lifted, yields the scent of old air, the kind that clings to pages turned yellow by the sun. Inside, objects crowd each other—a worn photograph, a spool of tape, a leaf pressed thin and fragile. Each piece a puzzle, a riddle from a past I do not own. Yet, I trace the edges with the care of one who knows, or perhaps, of one who chooses to believe. The sky shifts, a gentle reminder, as I find myself in the quiet embrace of stories not fully my own, yet undeniably close to my heart.
